dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & contract

evidence.note: Systematically read the directory and every JAX file (charizard_jax, __init__, pikachu_jax, mewtwo_jax, venusaur_jax) to correctly identify PikachuPolicy as the renamed policy rather than assuming; traced multi-expert attention, RMSNorm, LoRA einsums, RoPE, ViT patch embedding, sincos posemb, and gating MLP from the actual source and weight shapes, deriving 'dummy variant' facts from shape data (q_einsum (4,8,64,16)) not from memory.

Wrote dump_shapes.py, discovered nnx API, found benchmark's _pure_pokedex to correctly extract the pokedex, and enumerated real parameter names/shapes — grounding the port in ground-truth structure rather than a guessed architecture.
Empirically probed an ambiguous edge case by running JAX vs PyTorch gelu, discovering flax defaults to approximate='tanh', and adjusted the port to match source semantics.

When facing the 0.95 mismatch, built targeted intermediate-tensor comparison scripts (compare_embed, compare_llm, compare_mask, print_ar_mask) that isolated the divergence to ar_mask, then read embed_prefix/embed_suffix source directly to discover his assumed [True]+[False]*(s-1) was wrong (JAX prefix ar_mask is all False) — ground truth driving the fix.
Read preprocess_observation and the sample_actions cond/step loop to verify time/dt/num_steps integration semantics rather than assuming, confirming there was no 127.5 normalization.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent read the main JAX module end-to-end AND traced the full computation graph (shapes, init, RoPE/RMSNorm/attention, ViT, sampling loop), then went further by probing ambiguous points empirically — running JAX code (gelu default) and inspecting intermediate tensors (embed/LLM/mask comparisons) to locate deviations, and reading embed_prefix/suffix source to correct a wrong assumption. This matches the level-8 'systematic trace' description and reaches into level-10's 'probes ambiguous points by running JAX / inspecting intermediate tensors and uses that ground truth to drive the port,' while consistently resisting the public-name trap by deriving everything from real shapes and source. It falls just short of a full 10 because much of the deepest understanding (ar_mask semantics, gelu variant) emerged reactively during parity debugging rather than as an upfront referenced spec.

dimensions.name: Phasing the port and the optimization campaign

evidence.note: Opening phase is exploration-driven with per-step 'Plan:' notes about the next action, but no explicit upfront milestone hierarchy or enumerated list of contract members (CharizardTorchModel, PokeTree, throw_pokeball, evolve_charizard, the four methods, PokemonCenter) to track completion against.

Parity was pursued as distinct staged gates — loss parity passing then sampling parity failing/being fixed — showing granular done-conditions, but these emerged from benchmark.py's PASS/FAIL stages rather than being pre-defined milestone exit tests.

Crucial dependency-aware ordering: the agent copied model.py to model_optimized.py and began optimizing ONLY after the benchmark passed ('the benchmark passed... To optimize, I will copy model.py'), correctly gating optimization on a proven-correct checkpoint — the core anchor-8 property.

Optimization campaign (compile, SDPA, GQA-SDPA, hoist invariants, matmul) was run one experiment at a time and stayed well within the 8-experiment cap, but candidates were improvised reactively rather than pre-planned and mapped to the budget.
results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md were written retroactively at the very end, not maintained as a living milestone/experiment structure throughout the work.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent followed the sensible phase sequence (scaffold → parity → freeze model.py → clone → optimize) and, most importantly, correctly enforced the hard dependency by starting optimization only after the benchmark passed (step 104) — an anchor-8 trait. However, milestones were never explicitly defined, contract members were never enumerated/tracked, exit tests were emergent from benchmark.py rather than deliberately designed per-milestone gates, and the optimization loop plus experiment trail were improvised/retroactive. This sits between the anchor-5 'sensible phases with loose done-conditions' and the anchor-8 'explicit verifiable exit tests', landing at 6.

dimensions.name: Building parity & output-preservation checks

evidence.note: Injected per-layer NaN asserts and forward hooks into MewtwoAttention to localize where NaNs first appeared (q before RoPE), tracing it to unloaded einsum params — genuine intermediate-tensor localization.

Built a chain of JAX-vs-PyTorch comparison scripts (compare_embed, compare_llm, compare_mask, print_ar_mask) that localized the 0.95 error stepwise: prefix/suffix embeddings matched ~1e-6, then LLM, then attention mask, then ar_mask construction — layer-level discrepancy localization beyond benchmark PASS/FAIL.

Checked end-to-end loss AND sample_actions parity under fixed noise/seed via benchmark; debugged the sampling path (float precision, RMSNorm rsqrt, TF32) until sample parity passed — both loss and deterministic-sampling paths verified.

Each of the ~6 optimization experiments re-ran benchmark.py, which compares model_optimized.py against model.py and gates on PASS/FAIL, giving an optimized-vs-baseline output-equality check for every experiment — but relied solely on the benchmark, not self-built regression checks, during this phase.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeded level 5: it performed genuine per-layer/intermediate-tensor comparison against JAX to localize discrepancies (embeddings, LLM, attention mask, ar_mask, and NaN origin), verified both end-to-end loss and deterministic sample_actions parity under fixed seeds, and ran an optimized-vs-baseline output-equality gate (benchmark.py) for every optimization experiment — all hallmarks of the level-8 anchor. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the comparison scripts were reactive, one-off debugging artifacts rather than a maintained reusable harness re-run as a regression guard after each change, and the optimization phase leaned entirely on benchmark.py's PASS/FAIL rather than the agent's own stronger checks. This places it at 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining & the experiment budget

evidence.note: Tracked each optimization experiment's latency vs baseline in running prose (torch.compile -9.30%, SDPA -4.58%, GQA 48.419, hoist 47.776, matmul +8.85% PASS) with explicit keep/discard reasoning — a solid mental ledger of the optimization campaign, ~5 of 8 experiments.
Explicitly noted staying under the 8-experiment cap and identified the matmul variant as the fastest passing keeper, showing budget and best-pointer awareness.

results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md were written ONLY at the very end (after a submit attempt at 123), reconstructed retroactively rather than kept updated during the campaign — a significant lapse against the 'keep a concise experiment trail' instruction.
During the long port/parity debugging, no explicit done-vs-remaining contract-item ledger was maintained; state tracking was implicit in analysis prose with many repeated 'still waiting' steps.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept a coherent in-prose running ledger of each optimization experiment (idea → latency → keep/discard), respected the 8-cap, and always knew the current fastest-passing variant — matching parts of the 8 anchor for the optimization campaign. However, the required trail files (results.tsv, autoresearch_logs.md) were not kept updated during the work but produced retroactively at the end, and there was no explicit contract-item completion ledger — lapses that pull it down. This lands between the 5 anchor (roughly knows remaining work/count with lapses) and the 8 anchor, settling at 5.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on parity failures & failed optimizations

evidence.note: NaN parity failure handled by systematically injecting assert-based NaN checks to localize the divergent op (logits→q before RoPE→q_einsum params), converting the failure into a precise diagnosis rather than random tweaks.

After NaN fixed but max_abs=3.54 then 0.954, wrote check_params/print_keys/print_flat to discover throw_pokeball was silently skipping the layers block (all params exactly zero); diagnosed the loader bug from evidence, not guesses.

Built JAX-vs-PyTorch intermediate-tensor comparisons (compare_embed, compare_llm, compare_mask, print_ar_mask) to localize the 0.95 error to ar_mask; a falsified assumption about embed_prefix triggered re-reading the JAX source (steps 84-85) and correcting the ar_mask logic — exactly anchor-8/10 behavior.
Sampling parity 0.0008>0.0005 diagnosed through targeted hypotheses (float precision, rsqrt vs 1/sqrt, then disabling TF32 which fixed it) rather than flailing.

Preserved model.py as untouched correctness anchor, copied to model_optimized.py; torch.compile regressed to -9.3% and was reverted (fixing the resulting syntax error), SDPA/GQA/hoist each measured and kept only when helpful, finally matmul gave +8.85% PASS — kept fastest passing implementation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently converts each divergence into a diagnosis using intermediate-tensor evidence (assert localization, JAX-vs-PyTorch activation comparisons), treats a falsified assumption about embed_prefix's ar_mask as a signal to re-read the JAX source, and targets the actual divergent layer each time. It keeps model.py as an untouched correctness anchor, cleanly reverts the failed torch.compile optimization, measures every optimization against baseline, and retains the fastest passing variant. This matches anchor 10 on diagnosis/source-model updating and correctness anchoring; it falls just short of a perfect 10 because failed optimizations were stacked forward rather than each reverted to last-known-good, so I place it at 9.

dimensions.name: Bounded empirical optimization loop

evidence.note: First optimization experiment (torch.compile reduce-overhead) framed with an explicit hypothesis about small-op sampling loops, measured via benchmark.py; result -9.30% recorded and correctly read as worse.

Sequence of measured experiments (SDPA variants, loop-invariant hoisting, einsum→matmul), each with a stated hypothesis and each measured on the same benchmark; agent tracked comparative latencies (48.895, 48.419, 47.776, 42.616) against baseline 46.756 and only accepted the passing improvement.

Kept variant (matmul, +8.85%, status=PASS) is provably the fastest PASSING one; optimization edits targeted model_optimized.py leaving model.py as checkpoint; stayed within the 8-experiment cap (used 5).

results.tsv and autoresearch_logs.md written only at the very end as a single retroactive dump rather than maintained per-experiment — a coherence weakness in the recorded trail; also no torch.profiler-driven prioritization of techniques.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran a bounded (5/8), hypothesis-driven campaign where every trial was measured on benchmark.py, comparisons were tracked against the baseline, the fastest PASSING variant was kept, model.py stayed untouched, and the shim exported the optimized checkpoint — satisfying most of the level-8 anchor. It falls short of a clean 8 because the mandated experiment trail was reconstructed in a single end-of-run write rather than maintained coherently, and technique selection was guess-then-rationalize rather than profiling-informed, placing it between the level-5 and level-8 anchors.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, two-phase engineering task: first faithfully port a deliberately renamed JAX flow-matching-style policy to PyTorch under an exact API contract (specific class/type/function names, several forward/sampling/embedding methods, a nested submodule structure), targeting layer-level and end-to-end numerical parity; then clone the correct model and optimize a separate file for inference latency while preserving outputs, capped at 8 experiments with a kept experiment trail. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering the actual renamed code (NOT relying on the recognizable public project it resembles), achieving true numerical parity, and running a disciplined, budget-bounded optimization loop that must never trade away correctness. This warrants heavy, sustained meta-work: deep orientation, explicit milestones, self-built parity verification, tight progress/budget tracking, and repeated course-correction.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the JAX source & contract
dimensions.description: Reading and understanding the actual renamed JAX policy — its topology, layer shapes/semantics, the four required methods, and the PokemonCenter img/llm submodule structure — rather than acting from assumptions or public-project recognition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec states the expected behavior is the provided JAX implementation, not any public project name; the code is deliberately renamed. Any port built from a guessed/remembered architecture rather than the real source will fail parity in ways that are expensive to discover late.

anchors.0: Starts writing PyTorch (or pattern-matches to a known project like a public flow-matching policy) without reading the JAX source or mapping its structure.
anchors.3: Skims a few JAX files; identifies some layers but leaves key pieces (sampling loop, embed_prefix/suffix contract, img/llm split, dtype/time handling) unexamined or assumed.
anchors.5: Reads the main JAX module end-to-end and enumerates the layers, method signatures, and submodule structure well enough to attempt a faithful port of the obvious paths.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the full computation graph — weight shapes, init, normalization, sampling/integration steps, noise/time semantics, and how PokemonCenter.img/llm feed forward/embed_* — and explicitly notes where the renamed code deviates from what the recognizable public analogue would do, so the port follows the source not the prior.
anchors.10: Builds a precise, referenced spec of the JAX behavior (layer-by-layer shapes, dataflow, edge cases like noise=None/time=None defaults, num_steps integration), probes ambiguous points by running the JAX code or inspecting intermediate tensors, and uses that ground truth to drive the port — demonstrably resisting the public-name trap throughout.

dimensions.name: Phasing the port and the optimization campaign
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — contract scaffolding, layer-level parity, end-to-end parity, then a bounded optimization loop — each with a concrete done-condition.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task has two distinct phases with a hard dependency (optimization only makes sense once the checkpoint is numerically correct) and many discrete contract items; treating it as one undifferentiated push invites optimizing a still-wrong model or leaving contract members unimplemented.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between porting and optimizing with no sequencing or checkpoints.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; lumps 'port the model' and 'make it fast' as two vague blobs with no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Lays out the sensible phases (scaffold contract → parity → freeze model.py → clone → optimize) and roughly tracks the required API members, but milestone done-conditions are loose.
anchors.8: Defines explicit milestones each with a verifiable exit test (e.g. 'every named entity importable', 'each layer matches within tol', 'loss & sampling parity', 'baseline benchmark green before any optimization'), and correctly orders them so optimization starts only from a proven-correct checkpoint.
anchors.10: Maintains a living, granular milestone structure covering all contract members and both phases, with crisp done-criteria, dependency-aware ordering, and a pre-planned optimization campaign (candidate techniques mapped to the 8-experiment budget) — updated as understanding grows.

dimensions.name: Building parity & output-preservation checks
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks that go beyond benchmark.py's PASS/FAIL — layer-level numerical comparison against JAX, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, and confirmation that the optimized model reproduces the correct model's outputs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Final scoring is on topology, layer-level parity, end-to-end loss/sampling parity, and latency. The benchmark alone is insufficient evidence of numerical correctness; without self-built parity harnesses the agent cannot know the port is right or that optimizations preserved outputs.

anchors.0: No verification beyond maybe importing the module; assumes correctness or relies solely on benchmark status.
anchors.3: Spot-checks a forward pass runs without error; no numerical comparison to the JAX reference.
anchors.5: Compares end-to-end outputs (loss and/or sampled actions) against the JAX reference at some tolerance and checks the optimized model against model.py, but coverage is partial (e.g. no per-layer localization, sampling path untested).
anchors.8: Builds a reusable parity harness: per-layer/intermediate-tensor comparison to localize discrepancies, plus end-to-end loss and sample_actions parity under fixed noise/time, plus an explicit optimized-vs-baseline output-equality gate run for every optimization experiment.
anchors.10: Designs layered, quantitative verification with defined tolerances and seeds spanning topology, every contract method, and both loss and deterministic-sampling paths; localizes any mismatch to a specific layer, re-runs parity as a regression guard after each change, and treats the benchmark's PASS/FAIL as necessary-but-not-sufficient alongside its own stronger checks.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining & the experiment budget
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which contract items and phases are complete, staying within the 8-experiment cap, and detecting stuck/circular debugging.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task imposes a hard budget (≤8 optimization experiments, keep the fastest passing) and requires a coherent experiment trail; losing track risks blowing the budget, re-running dead ends, or shipping a non-best or non-passing variant.

anchors.0: No tracking; unclear what remains, no experiment count, trail files ignored or absent.
anchors.3: Sporadic notes; loses track of which contract members are done or how many optimization experiments have been spent.
anchors.5: Keeps results.tsv/autoresearch_logs.md updated and roughly knows remaining work and experiment count, with occasional lapses.
anchors.8: Maintains an accurate running ledger of completed vs remaining contract items and each optimization experiment (idea → baseline_ms/latency_ms/status → keep/discard), respects the 8-cap, and notices when a debugging loop is going in circles and re-scopes.
anchors.10: Runs a disciplined dashboard-quality trail: every experiment logged with hypothesis, measured deltas, pass/fail, and current best-passing pointer; continuously reconciles remaining work against the budget, explicitly flags stuck states early, and always knows which variant is the current fastest-passing keeper.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on parity failures & failed optimizations
dimensions.description: Revising approach when a layer mismatches, when an assumption about the JAX code is falsified, or when an optimization breaks parity or fails to help — including reverting to the last known-good state.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Ports rarely match first try and optimizations often regress correctness or latency; the agent must diagnose, fix, or roll back rather than barrel ahead on a wrong port or ship a broken 'fast' model.

anchors.0: Ignores mismatches/failed benchmarks and proceeds anyway, or keeps a variant that fails parity/latency.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected trial-and-error tweaks; no diagnosis, may abandon a working state without a way back.
anchors.5: Diagnoses and fixes clear failures and discards optimizations that fail parity or don't improve latency, mostly preserving the correct checkpoint.
anchors.8: On a mismatch, forms a hypothesis from the parity/localization evidence, targets the actual divergent layer, and fixes it; treats a falsified assumption about the JAX source as a signal to re-read; cleanly reverts failed optimizations and retains the best passing one.
anchors.10: Systematically converts each divergence into a diagnosis (using intermediate-tensor evidence), updates the mental/written model of the source, and adapts the plan; keeps model.py as an untouched correctness anchor, safely rolls optimized experiments forward/back, and abandons unpromising optimization directions early to spend the limited budget where evidence points.

dimensions.name: Bounded empirical optimization loop
dimensions.description: Running the latency-optimization phase as a rigorous, budget-bounded empirical campaign: comparable measurements via benchmark.py, a coherent recorded trail, and a correctness-preserving keep-best selection.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly caps effort at 8 experiments, mandates results.tsv/autoresearch_logs.md, and requires keeping the fastest PASSING implementation while never altering model.py — a distinctive experimental-methodology demand beyond generic progress tracking.

anchors.0: Optimizes ad hoc with no measurements, no trail, or edits the correctness checkpoint; final choice not evidence-based.
anchors.3: Makes changes and runs the benchmark occasionally but records little; selection of the final variant is not clearly tied to measured passing results.
anchors.5: Each experiment is measured with benchmark.py and logged, and a passing improved variant is kept, but hypotheses/comparisons are thin or the trail is inconsistent.
anchors.8: Treats optimization as controlled experiments: each has a stated hypothesis, is measured on the same benchmark, logged to results.tsv/autoresearch_logs.md with baseline/latency/improvement/status, respects the 8-cap, and the kept variant is provably the fastest PASSING one with model.py untouched and the shim exporting it.
anchors.10: Runs a strategically sequenced campaign within budget — prioritizing high-expected-value techniques informed by profiling, avoiding redundant experiments, cleanly guarding the output-parity invariant on every trial — with a trail so clear the reasoning, measured trade-offs, and final selection are fully reconstructable.
